stories.title: Introducing FrontierCode: a coding eval that raises the bar for difficulty & quality
stories.summary:
↳ WHAT'S NEW
Cognition released FrontierCode, a new coding benchmark designed to be harder and higher-quality than existing evals.

↳ THE REAL STORY
The source excerpt provides almost no usable detail — 'We made a thing!' is the entirety of the technical disclosure. Without knowing the task distribution, language coverage, difficulty calibration method, or how it compares to HumanEval, SWE-bench, or LiveCodeBench, there is nothing concrete to evaluate here. The benchmark may well be interesting, but the available content does not support any specific claims about what it measures or how it was constructed.
stories.considerations: The gap between the headline ('raises the bar for difficulty & quality') and the actual disclosed information ('We made a thing!') is worth noting. Cognition builds Devin, which means they have a direct commercial interest in how coding benchmarks are framed and which models score well on them. A benchmark released by a lab that also ships a coding agent warrants scrutiny around evaluation design, dataset contamination controls, and whether the tasks favor their own system's architecture. Wait for the technical report before drawing conclusions.

stories.title: Apple Unveils Next Generation of Apple Intelligence, Siri AI and More
stories.summary:
↳ WHAT'S NEW
Apple announced a next-generation Apple Intelligence and Siri AI suite at WWDC 2026, with details published on the Apple Newsroom.

↳ THE REAL STORY
The source excerpt cuts off mid-sentence, so the specific features, model names, and API changes aren't available here. What is available: the announcement exists, it's positioned as a generational step up from the 2024 Apple Intelligence rollout, and the person who flagged it is explicitly not taking the claims at face value. For developers building on-device or integrating Siri, the practical question isn't what Apple demoed on stage — it's what ships in the developer betas and whether the capability gap between announcement and release is smaller this time.
stories.considerations:
↳ WORTH WATCHING
The 2024 Apple Intelligence cycle was a case study in announcement-to-reality drift — features shown at WWDC either shipped late, shipped degraded, or didn't ship at all. The source author's 'I'll believe it when I see it' framing is the honest prior here. If you're making product or integration decisions based on this announcement, the beta developer build is the only document worth reading. Marketing copy from the Newsroom is not a spec.
